mcqs.question: A converging lens has a focal length of 20 cm. What is its power in dioptres?
mcqs.explanation: Power P = 1/f (where f is in metres). f = 20 cm = 0.20 m, so P = 1/0.20 = +5 D. Positive sign indicates a converging lens. Options C and D arise from mistakenly using centimetres directly, and option B has the wrong sign.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand combination of lens powers at the required level
mcqs.question: Two thin lenses are placed in contact. Lens 1 has a power of +3 D and Lens 2 has a power of –2 D. What is the total power of the combination?
mcqs.explanation: When lenses are in contact, their powers add algebraically: P_total = P1 + P2 = (+3) + (–2) = +1 D. Option A adds the magnitudes, while C and D give incorrect signs.

mcqs.question: A convex lens of focal length 10 cm is used. In case 1 the object is placed 15 cm from the lens; in case 2 the object is placed 30 cm from the lens. Which statement is true about the image distances?

options.A: The image distance in case 1 is greater than in case 2.
options.B: The image distance in case 2 is greater than in case 1.
options.C: The image distances are equal in both cases.
options.D: No real image forms in either case.

mcqs.answer: The image distance in case 1 is greater than in case 2.
mcqs.explanation:
Using 1/v = 1/f – 1/u (u is object distance):
Case 1: 1/v = 1/10 – 1/15 = 1/30 → v = 30 cm.
Case 2: 1/v = 1/10 – 1/30 = 2/30 → v = 15 cm.
Thus the image formed in case 1 is farther from the lens than in case 2. Options B, C, and D contradict the calculation.

mcqs.question: A concave lens has a focal length of –25 cm. A real object is placed 40 cm to the left of the lens. Using the Cartesian sign convention, what is the nature and position of the image?

options.A: Virtual image, 66.7 cm to the left of the lens
options.B: Real image, 66.7 cm to the right of the lens
options.C: Virtual image, 16.7 cm to the left of the lens
options.D: Real image, 16.7 cm to the right of the lens

mcqs.answer: Virtual image, 66.7 cm to the left of the lens
mcqs.explanation:
Using 1/v = 1/f – 1/u with sign convention: f = –25 cm, u = –40 cm.
1/v = –0.04 + 0.025 = –0.015 → v = –66.7 cm. Negative v indicates the image is on the same side as the object, i.e., a virtual image 66.7 cm left of the lens. Options B, C, and D give incorrect nature or distance.

mcqs.question: A convex lens of focal length 10 cm forms an image of an object placed 15 cm from the lens. What is the linear magnification of the image?
mcqs.explanation: First find image distance using the lens formula: 1/v = 1/10 – 1/15 = 1/30 → v = 30 cm. Magnification m = v/u = 30/15 = +2 (positive sign indicates an upright image in the sign‑convention used here). Option B has the wrong sign, and C and D are incorrect magnitudes.

mcqs.question: The power of a lens is defined as:

options.A: The reciprocal of its focal length in meters.
options.B: The focal length measured in centimeters.
options.C: The product of its focal length and refractive index.
options.D: The ratio of image distance to object distance.

mcqs.answer: The reciprocal of its focal length in meters.
mcqs.explanation: Power P (in dioptres) = 1/f where f is the focal length expressed in metres. This definition directly links the ability of a lens to converge or diverge light. Options B, C, and D describe unrelated quantities.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes the power (in dioptres) of a lens from its focal length (in centimetres)?

options.A: Power is the reciprocal of focal length in metres, while focal length is the distance at which parallel rays converge.
options.B: Power is measured in centimetres, while focal length is measured in dioptres.
options.C: Both power and focal length have the same numerical value but different units.
options.D: Power is the product of focal length and refractive index, whereas focal length is independent of material.

mcqs.answer: Power is the reciprocal of focal length in metres, while focal length is the distance at which parallel rays converge.
mcqs.explanation: Power (P) = 1/f (f in metres) gives a value in dioptres. Focal length is a geometric property measured in length units (cm or m). Options B and C invert the definitions, and D mixes up the lens maker's formula with the definition of power.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand combination of lens powers at the required level
mcqs.question: Two thin lenses are placed in contact: a converging lens of +4 D and a diverging lens of –2 D. What is the effective focal length of the combination?
mcqs.explanation: Combined power P_total = +4 D + (–2 D) = +2 D. Effective focal length f_eff = 1/P_total = 1/2 D = 0.5 m. Option B matches this result; the other options correspond to incorrect power sums.
